subject: Weekly executive readout + QBR prep — consolidated asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: exec-distro@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly executive readout + QBR prep — consolidated asks

Hi all,

Quick consolidated readout ahead of the QBR pack deadline next Friday. I pulled the cross-functional items that need leadership visibility or decisions this week. Read fast — bold asks at the bottom.

Wins
- Hosted API: latency P50 down 8% week-over-week after kernel update; cost/unit improved ~6% on steady workloads. Ops confirmed no regressions in the Canary group.
- Dedicated: closed two mid-market renewals (ACME & Lumen) with committed throughput uplifts; sales flagged more inbound interest in reserved capacity.
- Optimize: pilot batching recommendations reduced token cost for the top 3 customers on the plan by 11%.

Risks / Signals
- Capacity squeeze: north-south contention on A100 pools during EU prime hours has spiked tail latency for some Dedicated tenants. Engineering is evaluating an emergency scheduling tweak. Impact: potential SLA blips for 2 customers (ACME and a finance tenant) if unresolved by EOW.
- QBR narrative: our cost-per-inference slide needs a clearer story on batching gains vs. quantization tradeoffs — current draft overstates benefit in multi-tenant cases.
- Security/compliance: a customer SOC follow-up (ACME) requested a more granular token-retention timeline; that request dovetails with Private onboarding docs.

Asks (owners / ETA)
1) Capacity mitigation (owner: markus_klein) — decision on temporary A100 preemption windows or burst pool expansion. Need firm decision by 2027-06-22 COB so we can communicate to affected customers.
2) QBR deck clarity (owner: laura_bennett) — revise cost-per-inference slide to include a conservative multi-tenant uplift case and a footnote on quantization quality variance. Can you drop v2 in the Drive link by 2027-06-21 10:00 PT?
3) Customer SOC response (owner: hannah_schmitt) — I will coordinate with security to send the token-retention timeline. Need sign-off from legal on the wording by 2027-06-23.
4) Resource ask (owner: vivek_kulkarni) — we may need a short-term ops headcount (4 wks) for elevated hand-offs; estimate 0.4 FTE from Platform Eng. Please confirm capacity/alternatives.

Attachments: QBR-heatmap-v1 (see Drive).

If there are other blockers that should bubble up to the pack, flag them now.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

Hannah — re: capacity mitigation. A few data points:
- Short-term options: enable preemption windows on low-priority jobs (risk: slightly higher tail for batch-heavy internal workloads) OR spin a temporary burst pool (cost ~2.5% of current monthly infra spend for the region).
- Long term: prioritize tenant-aware KV caching & autoscale tuning for Dedicated (Q3 item).

If leadership is inclined to avoid bill increases, the preemption approach is faster and reversible. If we choose burst capacity, Ops needs a nod by 2027-06-22 morning to provision.

Question for Vivek: do we have the budget headroom for a 4-week ops augmentation (Hannah estimates 0.4 FTE) without impacting Q3 hiring plans?

Markus

Redwood Inference
